current_evidence: The workbook PDF is on enfield.gov.uk and its cover reads 'Local Validation Requirements for planning applications 28th September 2026'. It replaces the 25th March 2024 edition (asset 47918), which the council's planning-application-guidance page still links as 'updated as of 14 October 2024'. That page and planning.data.gov.uk do not yet link the 2026 PDFs, so the date it takes effect could not be confirmed from a linking page.

issues.detail: The tab mixes the 2026 lists with superseded editions. Several tab_items come from the 25 March 2024 non-householder list (asset 47918), including the drawing standards, the SPA/SAC/SAMM text and the viability text. Others come from the old single-family-dwellings list (asset 47919, Nov 2023), including the 1:50 plan rules, hardstanding and the 21-day withdrawal rule. They are not marked as superseded.
issues.evidence: 47918 cover: '25th March 2024'; guidance page: major/minor list 'updated as of 14 October 2024', single family dwellings 'updated as of 6 November 2023'

issues.detail: The same text appears twice because it was taken from both the old and the new list. The un-redacted viability assessment sentence comes from both 47918 and 141100 (with 'Page 26 of 63' embedded). The 21-day withdrawal/administration-fee sentence comes from both 47919 and 47918.
issues.evidence: 'You should send an un-redacted affordable housing financial viability ... assessment' appears in both PDFs

issues.detail: Grokbot has no Transport Assessment for any application type. The source requires one for major developments and adds Healthy Streets and other items where a major creates 50 or more residential units. A Highway Safety Impact Assessment is also missing. Its trigger is minor developments creating new residential and/or commercial units, changes of use, and commercial/community/industrial extensions.
issues.evidence: Local requirements checklist items 15 'Highway Safety Impact Assessment' and 23 'Transport Assessment: major developments'

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment and the Sustainable Drainage Strategy (SuDS) appear only under Householder, not for non-householder applications. The FRA applies to changes of use creating new residential/commercial units, to sites in specified flood zones or at surface water risk, and to development within 8m of a watercourse. SuDS applies to major developments, commercial/industrial changes of use or new buildings, new residential buildings, basement extensions and ground-level extensions.
issues.evidence: Checklist items 14 'Flood Risk Assessment' and 21 'Sustainable Drainage Strategy (SuDS)'

issues.detail: Several local requirements on the non-householder list were not captured at all. Contaminated Land Assessment: proposals on potentially contaminated land, such as former landfill, railway land or petrol stations. Tall Building Statement: buildings over 6 storeys or 18m. Marketing Assessment: loss of public houses, community facilities, Class E commercial space or industrial uses, or change of use of Listed Buildings.
issues.evidence: Checklist items 7, 18 and 22; 'All applications for tall buildings, those over 6 storeys or 18m in height'

issues.detail: Some requirements are captured only under Householder but are also on the non-householder list, where Grokbot omits them. Archaeological Assessment: extensive demolition or groundworks within an Archaeological Priority Area, heritage-asset sites, majors over 0.5ha, and EIA screening/scoping. Noise and Ventilation Impact Assessment: residential and other noise-sensitive development close to existing noise sources. Tree Assessment: removal or pruning of trees or hedges in a Conservation Area or under a TPO, or groundworks within 15m of trees. Existing/proposed roof plans and sections (Section Two plans items 4 and 5) are also missing.
issues.evidence: Checklist items 2, 19 and 24; Section Two plans items 4 'Existing and Proposed Roof Plan' and 5 'Existing and Proposed Sections'

issues.detail: Grokbot has the Epping Forest SAC Recreation Mitigation Strategy only as a generic 'Habitats Regulations Assessment' row, with the trigger 'a project-level HRA screening and where necessary, appropriate assessment'. The source trigger is any proposal creating new residential units within the Zone of Influence, with SAMM/SANG payment and an SAC agreement form. The source applies it to Full, Outline, Reserved Matters, discharge of pre-commencement conditions, prior approval/PD and minor amendments, not only Full planning.
issues.evidence: 'Proposals creating new residential* units within the identified Zone of Influence'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are cut-off fragments or table-of-contents text rather than the actual trigger. BNG (Full) reads 'Guidance on biodiversity net gain Glossary ... SECTION ONE'; the source says major development from 12 Feb 2024 and minor from 2 Apr 2024, subject to exemptions. Planning Statement (Householder and Full) is contents-page boilerplate. Energy reads 'with their energy Statement.'; the source covers minor developments creating new residential/commercial units, majors, and extensions of 250m2 or more. Viability reads 'in the viability appraisal.'; the source covers majors, affordable housing triggers, enabling development, and cases relying on viability. CIL reads 'see where CIL charges apply.'; the source says 100m2 or more of new floorspace or one or more new dwellings. Telecoms reads 'Radiation Protection (ICNIRP).'. Floor plans reads 'the proposed floor plans'. The Daylight/Sunlight excerpt runs on into the Electronic Communications section.
issues.evidence: Checklist item 6 'Community Infrastructure Levy Information: 100m2 or more new floorspace, or one or more new dwellings'; item 10 Energy Assessment trigger

issues.detail: The Full-planning Design and Access Statement excerpt stops at 'Required for all applications: The Town and Country Planning (Development'. This suggests a DAS is always required. The source limits it to Conservation Areas with 100m2 or more of new floorspace, or proposals affecting the setting of a Listed Building, historic park/garden or Scheduled Monument (plus major development under national rules).
issues.evidence: Section One item 4 Design and Access Statement

issues.detail: Some requirements are mislabelled. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is the Structural Method Statement/Survey, which applies to substantial works where the retained structure changes significantly, there is a basement, or foundations are affected. The Householder 'Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment' row is a Heritage Statement cross-reference sentence. The Full 'Ecological Survey' excerpt is BNG declaration text, not the Biodiversity/Ecology Assessment trigger (development within or affecting designated sites or wildlife corridors). The Householder 'Ventilation/Extraction (odour)' row is the Noise and Ventilation Impact Assessment.
issues.evidence: 'Structural Method Statement / Survey When Expected: Required for all applications involving substantial works...'

issues.detail: Most Full-planning rows are flagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. The 2026 document covers all non-householder types and has a per-type grid (Full, Outline, LBC, Advert, CLU, Prior Notification, RM, S73, Approval of Details, Tree Works, S96A). Two rows are clearly misplaced: Advertisement drawings/illumination belongs to Advertisement Consent, and Telecoms supplementary information belongs to mast/antenna prior approvals. Grokbot shows Outline, Reserved Matters, LBC, S73, Discharge, NMA and Prior approval as '(none)', yet the source applies items such as the Epping Forest SAC strategy to them and has type-specific guidance for Outline, LBC, CLU, S73/S96A and Tree Works.
issues.evidence: 'Guidance on validation requirements by application type'; grid columns Full/Outline/LBC/Advert/CLU/Prior Notification/RM/S73/Approval of Details/Tree Works/S96A

issues.detail: Several tab_items are process text, boilerplate or fragments, not requirements: 'validated within 5 working days of receipt'; the 21-day withdrawal/administration fee (twice); 'remove any personal data you do not want published'; 'Protecting Your Information'; 'we will refund your SAMMs/SANGs payment after 6 months'; and the bare list fragment 'Special Protection Area (SPA)** Special Area of Conservation (SAC) ** Ramsar Site Nationally designated sites'. The Householder and Full 'Pre-application advice' rows describe the optional pre-application service, not a validation requirement.
issues.evidence: 'If the correct requirements are provided, your application will be validated within 5 working days of receipt.'

issues.detail: Grokbot presents Construction Management Plan, Statement of Community Engagement, Economic Statement, Health Impact Assessment, Utilities/foul sewage, Open space, Photographs/Photomontages and Designing Out Crime as standalone requirements. In the source they appear as 'When Expected' content within the Planning Statement guidance in Section Three, not in the 24-item local requirements checklist. The trigger text Grokbot quotes is accurate.
issues.evidence: 'Construction Management Plan (CMP) When Expected: Proposals involving major developments and/or commercial/community/industrial extensions of 250m2 or greater'

summary: Grokbot's link points to the newest official Enfield list (cover dated 28 September 2026), but the guidance page still links the March 2024 edition. The tab mixes superseded 2023/2024 text with the 2026 list. It misses major local requirements for non-householder applications (Transport Assessment, Highway Safety, FRA/SuDS, Contaminated Land, Tall Building Statement, Marketing, Archaeology, Noise, Tree Assessment), and many triggers are fragments.

withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The workbook stores all list dates at month precision (YYYY-MM-01), so 2026-09-01 correctly reflects the 28 September 2026 cover; the only valid point is that Date_basis says 'url' when the cover text could be cited.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
